title: Getting going with Go
course_section: Course introduction, Getting going with Go

hints.TestGreeting: Just put an emoji like 😃 or 🌴 in the string. Go source files are UTF-8.
hints.TestRawLiteral: Wrap the text in backticks (`...`) instead of double quotes so \n stays as two characters.
hints.TestByteAndRuneCount: len(s) gives bytes; utf8.RuneCountInString(s) (package unicode/utf8) gives runes.
hints.TestCodePoints: Range over the string to get runes, and use fmt.Sprintf("%U", r).

quiz.q: Which function is the entry point of a Go executable?
quiz.why: A program is the main package plus its imports, and execution begins at func main.
len counts bytes. Each of those characters takes 3 bytes in UTF-8.

quiz.q: What is the type `rune` an alias for?
quiz.why: A rune is a Unicode code point stored as an int32. A byte is a uint8.

quiz.q: What does the parameter `a ...any` in fmt.Println mean?
options: exactly one argument of any type
a slice that must be passed with ...
zero or more arguments of any type
quiz.why: It is a variadic parameter of the empty interface type.

quiz.q: Which is a raw string literal?
quiz.why: Backticks create raw string literals: escape sequences are not processed.
